transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I... I hope I'm not taking up time that someone else might need more, but my wife really wanted me to come in. 

I guess I'm here because... well, I had a bit of an out-of-character moment at work recently. I'm the chief executive of my company, and normally I pride myself on being very level-headed, you know? But we were on a board call, and someone asked a very minor, routine question about the facility budget, and I just... I snapped at them. I raised my voice, and I was quite sharp. 

It wasn't a huge deal, I apologized right after, but... it's just not how I run my company or how I treat people. I suppose I've just been feeling a little more on edge lately. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing people come here for?
Have you noticed any other changes in your mood or behavior lately, such as feeling more irritable, anxious, or having trouble sleeping?

Well, I... I suppose I have been a little more tired than usual, but nothing too out of the ordinary for someone in my position. I mean, running a company is demanding, right? It's normal to have a few restless nights here and there when you have a lot on your plate. 

As for being anxious... I wouldn't use that word, exactly. Maybe just a bit more focused on making sure everything is running smoothly. I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything. I'm still handling my responsibilities. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. I hope I'm answering your questions correctly?
Have you noticed yourself losing interest or not getting as much pleasure from things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with family?

Well, I... I don't want to sound ungrateful or anything. I have a very good life, and I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do. But I suppose, if I'm being completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information here—some things have felt a little different. 

Usually, I have a few things that really settle me down after a long day. Working on a chess problem, going through my hiking notes, or just having a nice dinner with my wife. But right now, they just feel a bit... flat, I guess. It’s like I know in my head that I should be enjoying them, but I just can't quite get there. 

I'm sure it's just a temporary phase, though. Everyone gets a little preoccupied and loses their spark for a week or two, don't they? I hope that answers what you were asking.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, recently?

Oh, no, no. I wouldn't use the word depressed. I mean... I really don't want to give you the wrong impression here. I’m not sitting around feeling sad or sorry for myself all day. I’ve worked very hard to build my company, and I’m incredibly grateful for everything I have. 

I know you have to ask these things, and I want to be as helpful as I can, but... no, I'm not feeling down like that. Just a little out of sorts and flat, like I mentioned. I hope it’s alright that I don’t check that particular box for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right picture of what's going on.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or feeling fatigued more often than usual, even when you haven’t been physically active?

Well, like I said earlier, I have been a little more tired than usual. But... I wouldn't call it a loss of energy, exactly. I mean, I'm still getting up, going to the office, handling my meetings. I'm not just lying in bed all day, if that's what you mean. 

I suppose maybe I feel a bit more drained at the end of the day than I normally would, even if I've just been sitting at my desk. But again, I think that's pretty standard for someone carrying a lot of responsibility, isn't it? It's just a bit of mental fatigue. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea here. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions lately, even with things that you would normally find straightforward?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I'm having trouble concentrating, no. I mean, my work requires a lot of focus, and I'm still managing everything just fine. I haven't dropped the ball on any major decisions or anything like that. I want to be clear about that, because I know how important it is to give you accurate information. 

Maybe sometimes it takes me an extra minute or two to review a contract, or I have to read an email twice to make sure I've got the tone right. But that's just being thorough, isn't it? I wouldn't call it a difficulty, really. Just... being careful. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I really don't want to make it seem like I can't handle my responsibilities.
Have you found it harder to think clearly or make decisions lately, even about things you normally wouldn't give a second thought to?

Well, I think... I mean, you just asked about concentrating and decisions, right? I feel like my answer is pretty much the same there. I wouldn't say it's harder to think clearly. I'm still steering the ship at work, still making the calls that need to be made. 

I really don't want to give the impression that my mind is slipping or anything like that. I'm just as sharp as ever, maybe just a little... preoccupied, given everything. But nothing that stops me from functioning normally. I hope that's okay? I just want to be sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking without making things sound worse than they actually are.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm definitely not moving in slow motion or anything. I mean, I keep a pretty brisk pace at the office, walking from meeting to meeting. I'm not dragging my feet. 

And as for being restless... well, maybe I tap my pen on the desk every now and then, or shift in my chair, but I wouldn't call it an inability to sit still. It's just normal nervous energy, right? The kind anyone gets when they have a lot on their plate. I can definitely sit through a long board meeting without jumping out of my skin. I hope that's the kind of detail you need? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, that I'm keeping it all together.

You mentioned that some things feel a bit flat and that you know you should be enjoying them but can't quite get there. Has this happened with activities you used to really enjoy, like working on chess problems or having dinner with your wife, or has it mostly been with newer or less meaningful activities?

Well, I suppose... yes, it's mostly with the things I usually rely on to unwind. Like, normally, if I sit down with a good chess problem or look over my hiking notes, it settles me right down. Or even just having a nice dinner with my wife. Those are the things I've always enjoyed. 

But lately, they just feel... flat, I guess. Like, I'm sitting there, and I know I *should* be enjoying it, but I just can't quite get there. It's not that I'm miserable or anything like that! I don't want you to think I'm depressed or completely checked out. I'm still doing all those things, still showing up for dinner. It's just... the spark isn't quite there right now. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea without making it sound like I'm falling apart, because I'm really not.
How long have you been feeling this way, with things feeling flat and less enjoyable than usual?

Well, I suppose... it's been about six days now. Ever since the, um... the explosion and the fire during that site walkthrough I was on. 

I mean, it hasn't been a long time at all, really. Just under a week. I'm sure it's just a temporary blip, you know? Anyone would feel a little off after something like that, right? I'm sure I'll bounce back and be enjoying things again in no time. I just don't want to make too big a deal out of a few days of feeling a little disconnected. Does that sound like a normal reaction to you? I hope I'm not overreacting by even bringing it up.
Since the explosion and fire last week, have you experienced any other changes in how you feel, besides things feeling flat or less enjoyable?

No, not really. I mean, other than that little bit of flatness we just talked about, I feel pretty much like myself. I'm not walking around angry or... or breaking down or anything like that. I've always been a steady guy. You have to be in my position, you know? 

So, no, no other big changes in how I feel. I hope that's a good sign? Like, that means I'm handling it alright, doesn't it? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right, but I really do think I'm doing okay, all things considered. I'm definitely not falling apart on you.
Since the explosion and fire last week, have you had any unwanted or intrusive memories of the event, or found yourself avoiding certain places or situations because of it?

Well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there have been a few moments. It's not like it's taking over my life or anything! I'm still getting all my work done. But... sometimes, right in the middle of a call, or when I'm just sitting there looking at numbers on a spreadsheet, the blast... and that fire by the loading area... they just sort of jump back into my head. 

It's like a bad film I didn't ask to see, you know? Just a quick flash, and then I push it right back down and get back to work. I haven't been avoiding going anywhere, though. I mean, I have a company to run, I can't just hide away. So I'm still doing everything I need to do. It's just those little flashes every now and then. That's pretty normal after something like this, right? Just the brain sort of processing things? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I really am handling it fine.
Do these intrusive memories of the explosion and fire cause you significant distress or interfere with your ability to focus on your work or other daily activities?

Well, I wouldn't say they cause significant distress, no. I'm still technically working, still showing up every day and putting in the hours. But... I suppose, if I'm looking at it honestly to make sure I'm giving you the right picture... I have been sort of... delaying some decisions about the facility. Just putting them off a bit. 

And I've been leaning on my team a lot more for calls that I would normally handle myself. I mean, it's good to delegate sometimes, right? A good boss trusts his people. But, um... we had a board call recently, and my reaction on it... well, it kind of made me realize that this might be starting to affect my judgment a little bit. My leadership, I guess. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm not capable of doing my job, because I am! I built myself up to this position, and I know how to run things. It's just a temporary thing, right? Taking a step back for a few days to get my head straight and let the team handle the heavy lifting... that makes sense after something like this, doesn't it? I just hope I'm doing the right thing by taking it a little easy.
Since the explosion and fire last week, have you felt numb, detached, or less aware of your surroundings at any point?

Well, no, not numb. I wouldn't use that word. I'm definitely still plugged in and aware of what's going on around me. 

But... I guess there have been a couple of odd moments. Just little things, really nothing major. Like, sometimes when I'm taking those calls from home... the room just sort of... I don't know, it looks a little distant? And my own voice sounds a bit strange to me. Almost like... like I'm watching myself talk on the call, instead of actually being the one talking. 

It's really hard to explain, and it sounds a lot crazier than it actually is. It passes pretty quick. I think it's just fatigue, you know? Just being tired and stressed from dealing with the aftermath of the fire. That's a pretty normal reaction to being overworked, right? Just a little bit of burnout making things feel a bit off for a second? I'm sure it's nothing to worry about.

Since the explosion and fire, have you felt detached from others or experienced a persistent negative emotional state, such as anger, guilt, or a loss of interest in things that used to matter a lot to you?

Well, no, not angry or guilty. I mean, accidents happen, and I'm not the type to sit around pointing fingers or beating myself up. And I wouldn't say I've lost interest in my life or anything drastic like that. 

But... I suppose, just to be completely transparent with you... things have felt a little... flat lately. Just a bit muted, I guess you could say. Usually, when I want to unwind after a long day, I'll work on a chess problem, or look over my old hiking notes, or just have a nice quiet dinner with my wife. Those things always settle me right down. 

Lately, though... I do them, and I know I should be enjoying them, but... I just can't quite get there. It's like the feeling is just out of reach. It's not that I don't care about my wife or my hobbies! I really do. It's just... maybe my brain is just too full right now with the business and the cleanup to really relax and enjoy things? That makes sense, doesn't it? Just a temporary inability to switch off because there's so much on my plate? I'm sure once things settle down at the facility, I'll be right back to my old self.
Since the explosion and fire, have you noticed a significant decrease in your ability to feel pleasure, even in activities you usually enjoy the most?

Well, I wouldn't say there's a *significant* decrease. Like I was just saying, I'm still doing the things I usually do. Still sitting down for dinner, still pulling out the chess board. 

I guess... maybe it's just that I'm not getting that same spark from them right this minute. It's not that I can't feel pleasure at all! I mean, I still appreciate a good meal and I still love spending time with my wife. It's just... a little harder to really sink into it and enjoy it fully right now. 

But that's just because my mind is still racing with work, you know? It's hard to feel completely relaxed and happy when you've got a major crisis at the facility hanging over your head. Anyone would feel a little distracted and less joyful under these circumstances, wouldn't they? I'm just trying to stay focused on getting things back to normal, and I figure the enjoyment of the little things will come back once the big things are sorted out. That sounds about right, doesn't it?
How many days out of the past two weeks have you felt down, depressed, or experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy?

Gosh, counting the days... I really couldn't give you a number. And, well, "depressed" is a pretty strong word, isn't it? I definitely wouldn't say I've been depressed. I'm not, you know, moping around or anything like that. I'm still up at dawn, still running the business, still getting things done. 

Like I was just saying, it's really just that things feel a little flat sometimes when I try to relax in the evenings. But it's not an all-day thing, and it's certainly not every day. Just... here and there since the fire. 

It's really just the stress talking, I'm sure. You see guys in my position get a little worn down and distracted like this all the time, right? It's perfectly normal to not be jumping for joy when you're managing a crisis, don't you think?
Have you felt down or experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy for most of the day, on more days than not, in the past two weeks?

Well, like I was trying to explain just a minute ago... I really wouldn't say it's most of the day, or even more days than not. When I'm at the facility, I'm locked in, getting the cleanup done and managing the crew. I'm not feeling down while I'm working. 

It's really just... well, like I mentioned before, it's those evening routines. The things that usually settle me, you know? Sitting down with a chess problem, or flipping through my old hiking notes, or just having that quiet dinner with my wife. They just feel... flat right now. I sit there, and I know in my head that I should be enjoying them, but I just can't get there. 

But again, that's just at the end of the day when I'm completely worn out, not all day long. That's pretty standard when a guy is working long hours to fix a big mess, isn't it? I mean, you don't think it's anything more serious than just being exhausted from the business, do you?
Would you say that, since the fire, you’ve experienced a noticeable drop in your ability to feel pleasure, even in the activities you normally enjoy the most?

Well, doctor, I... I know we kind of just touched on this, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers here. 

Like I was trying to explain a minute ago, it's really just those things that usually settle me down. You know, working out a chess problem, looking over my old hiking notes, or just having dinner with my wife. Lately they just feel... flat right now. I sit there, and I know I should be enjoying them, but I just can't quite get there. 

But I wouldn't want you to think it's some huge, terrible drop-off, you know? It's not like I'm broken or anything like that. It's just a little harder to find the joy while we're cleaning up the mess at the facility. That's a pretty normal reaction for a guy carrying a lot of responsibility, wouldn't you say? I hope I'm making sense.
Since the fire, have you found that almost nothing gives you pleasure, even things you usually enjoy very much?

Well, doctor, I... I feel like I'm giving you the same answer again, and I really don't want to be difficult. I hope I'm answering this the right way for you. 

It's not that *nothing* gives me pleasure. I mean, I'm still getting satisfaction out of a hard day's work at the site. It's just... well, like I said, it's those quiet things. The things that usually settle me down at night. Sitting with a chess problem, or looking over my hiking notes, or even just having dinner with my wife. They just feel flat right now. I sit there, and I know I should be enjoying them, but I just can't get there. 

But I wouldn't say it's almost nothing, you know? I don't want to paint a picture that I'm completely miserable. It's just a temporary thing while I'm dealing with the stress of the fire, right? That's what you'd expect to see in a guy in my position, isn't it?
